titleEn: Stop losing yield — and money — to wet fields
titleZh: 停止因湿田而损失产量和金钱
summaryZh: 本文报道了Grand Farm Cultivate会议上专家关于农田水分过多管理的讨论。专家指出，过量水分会导致根系缺氧、养分流失、病害增加等问题。解决方案包括：利用覆盖作物加速水分蒸发、安装排水暗管、根据土壤类型（沙土/黏土）采取不同策略、以及数据驱动的精准决策。文章强调没有单一解决方案，需要综合农艺、工程、管理和技术。
featuredReason: 本文虽非直接聚焦智慧畜牧，但覆盖作物、排水暗管、数据驱动决策等水分管理策略对智慧畜牧中的牧草种植、饲料田管理及牧场水土保持具有重要参考价值，体现了精准农业与可持续发展的结合。

Stop losing yield — and money — to wet fields

Try drainage tiling, cover crop tactics and other strategies to mitigate excess soil moisture.

Sarah McNaughton-Peterson,Senior Editor,Dakota FarmerJuly 23, 2026

schedule3 Min Read

Excess soil moisture can cause extreme detriments to a successful crop, as plant roots can fail to get oxygen, or applied nutrients can run off before they reach crop roots and cause a litany of other management issues for farmers. Take a multifaceted approach to protect crops from excess soil moisture. Henry Arden/Getty Images

Farming depends on a few inches of topsoil and the right amount of moisture to be successful. But what happens when farmers are met with the challenge of too much water?

A panel of agriculture experts weighed in on how farmers can manage too much moisture during Grand Farm’s Cultivate conference in Fargo, N.D. From drain tiles and cover crops to precision technology and more, finding a solution can take numerous paths.

“Our growers today are challenged for time. The windows are tight, so excess moisture makes decision-making extremely tough,” said Derrik Ellingson of Ellingson Companies. “Nothing’s cheap anymore. Fertilizer costs are at the highest they’ve ever been.”

Coupled with high fuel costs and higher production costs, excess moisture really poses a threat to farms’ bottom line. It can deprive plant roots of oxygen, stunt plant growth, cause nutrient run-off, bring soluble salts to the topsoil, and predispose plants to have rotten roots. So, what solutions are out there?

Related:How to prepare for drought conditions

Marisol Berti, a professor at North Dakota State University, explained one option growers can utilize.

“We can move water from the soil to the atmosphere with plants,” she said. “If we don’t have any green cover or plants, the water just doesn’t move in the soil.”

Examples Berti cited from her experiences with cover crops showed the power of plants.

“I’ve seen a farmer where they got 4 inches of rain, but he had cover crops and could work the next day,” she said. “A field that had been tilled, had no cover crops and had gotten 4 inches of rain? There’s no way they’d be able to work in that field.”

Finding a path forward

Berti said you have to think systematically about management strategies.

“We have to think of the diversity of the crops that we grow, and try to integrate these cover crops where we can,” she added.

Data-driven decision-making can help farmers navigate water management challenges.

“There’s no one-size-fits-all solution,” said Jeremiah Roeth, founder and CEO of Aerial Plot. “It has a lot to do with how much water comes, what happened before the water [and] what growth stage the crop is at.”

Soil type of an affected field also plays a large role in how water is managed. Sandy soils drain quickly, while clay soils hold water, and both require different application and water management strategies.

Drainage tiling is an option for long-term water management, but it requires a higher up-front investment. When drainage tile is installed beneath fields, it moves gravitational water that soil cannot hold, allowing oxygen to aerate the soil profile.

Related:How to keep up with recordkeeping on your farm

“We’ve had customers who talk about how much better the yields were with the deeper roots to be able to get in that farm sooner and plant it sooner,” Ellingson said. “Getting into the field in that window is what really could make or break it.”

Taking a collaborative approach with management strategies and neighboring farms means everyone can succeed. Communal ditch systems and water channels can move water appropriately without causing downstream flooding.

As the panel discussion concluded, the experts agreed that the future of strategic water management doesn’t lie in any single technology or practice, but in the deliberate integration of agronomy, engineering, stewardship and technology.

About the Author

Sarah McNaughton-Peterson

Senior Editor, Dakota Farmer

Sarah McNaughton-Peterson of Bismarck, N.D., has been editor of Dakota Farmer since 2021. Before working at Farm Progress, she was an NDSU 4-H Extension agent in Cass County, N.D. Prior to that, she was a farm and ranch reporter at KFGO Radio in Fargo.

She is a graduate of North Dakota State University, with a bachelor’s degree in ag communications and a master’s in Extension education and youth development.

She is involved in agriculture in both her professional and personal life, as a member of North Dakota Agri-Women, Agriculture Communicators Network, Sigma Alpha Professional Agriculture Sorority Alumni and Professional Women in Agri-business. As a life-long 4-H’er, she is a regular volunteer for North Dakota 4-H programs and events.

In her free time, she and her husband are avid backpackers and hikers, and can be found most summer weekends at rodeos around the Midwest.

translationZh:
农田耕作依赖于几英寸的表层土壤和适量的水分才能成功。但当农民面临水分过多的挑战时，会发生什么？

在Grand Farm于北达科他州法戈举办的Cultivate会议上，一组农业专家就农民如何管理过多水分发表了看法。从排水暗管和覆盖作物到精准技术等，寻找解决方案可以有很多途径。

“我们的种植者如今时间紧迫。作业窗口很窄，因此过多水分使决策变得极其困难，”Ellingson Companies的Derrik Ellingson说。“现在什么都不便宜。肥料成本处于历史最高水平。”

加上高昂的燃料成本和更高的生产成本，过多水分确实对农场的盈利构成威胁。它会使植物根系缺氧、抑制植物生长、导致养分流失、将可溶性盐带到表土层，并使植物容易发生烂根。那么，有哪些解决方案呢？

北达科他州立大学教授Marisol Berti解释了种植者可以利用的一种选择。

“我们可以通过植物将水分从土壤转移到大气中，”她说。“如果我们没有绿色覆盖或植物，水分在土壤中就无法移动。”

Berti引用她在覆盖作物方面的经验实例，展示了植物的力量。

“我见过一位农民，那里下了4英寸的雨，但他种了覆盖作物，第二天就能下地作业，”她说。“一块经过翻耕、没有覆盖作物、也下了4英寸雨的地呢？他们根本不可能在那块地里作业。”

**寻找前进之路**

Berti说，必须系统地考虑管理策略。

“我们必须考虑所种植作物的多样性，并尝试在可能的地方整合这些覆盖作物，”她补充道。

数据驱动的决策可以帮助农民应对水分管理挑战。

“没有一刀切的解决方案，”Aerial Plot创始人兼首席执行官Jeremiah Roeth说。“这在很大程度上取决于来了多少水、水来之前发生了什么、以及作物处于什么生长阶段。”

受影响田地的土壤类型也在水分管理中起着重要作用。沙质土壤排水快，而黏质土壤保水性强，两者需要不同的施用和水分管理策略。

排水暗管是长期水分管理的一种选择，但需要较高的前期投资。当排水暗管安装在田地下方时，它会移动土壤无法保持的重力水，使氧气能够进入土壤剖面。

“我们有客户谈到，由于根系更深，能够更早进入农田并更早播种，产量提高了多少，”Ellingson说。“在那个窗口期进入田地，才是真正决定成败的关键。”

采取协作的管理策略并与邻近农场合作，可以使每个人都成功。公共沟渠系统和水道可以适当地移动水分，而不会导致下游洪水。

随着小组讨论的结束，专家们一致认为，未来战略性水分管理的关键不在于任何单一技术或实践，而在于农艺、工程、管理和技术的刻意整合。
contentHtml: Try drainage tiling, cover crop tactics and other strategies to mitigate excess soil moisture.
